q: Electrolytic process is the use of electrolysis by which ____ are decomposed when an electric current is passed through them.
e: Electrolysis decomposes ionic substances into their constituent elements or simpler compounds.

q: It is commercially important as a stage in the ____ using an electrolytic cell.
c: separation of elements from minerals and ores
e: Electrolysis is widely used in metallurgy to extract and refine metals from their ores.

q: When an electric current is passed through the ____, the chemical reactions take place at the electrodes.
e: Molten salts contain free mobile ions that can migrate to the electrodes and undergo redox reactions.

q: At ____, sodium chloride is melted.
e: High temperatures are required to overcome the strong ionic bonds in solid sodium chloride to melt it.

q: This molten or fused sodium chloride contains ____ ions.
e: Molten sodium chloride dissociates into sodium cations and chloride anions.

q: On electrolysis, $Na^+$ ions accept electrons and discharge at the ____ and $Cl^-$ ions give up electrons and discharge at the anode.
e: Positive sodium ions migrate to the negative cathode to gain electrons and form sodium metal.

q: Net result: ____ floats to the top of the melt above the cathode and is drained off into a storage tank.
e: Sodium metal is less dense than the molten salt, so it floats to the top for collection.

q: ____ bubbles out of the melt above the anode.
e: Chloride ions are oxidised at the anode to form chlorine gas.

q: Aqueous salt solutions contain cations and anions from the ____ of salt and some $H^+$ and $OH^-$ ions from slight dissociation of water.
e: Salts completely dissociate in water, while water itself slightly dissociates into $H^+$ and $OH^-$ ions.

q: In an aqueous solution of electrolyte, there are usually ____.
c: more than one species of cation(positive ion) or anion (negative ion)
e: Aqueous solutions contain ions from both the dissolved solute and the water solvent.

q: The preferential discharge of these ions depends on the following three factors: ____, the concentration of electrolyte and the nature of the electrode used.
c: position of metal ions or groups in the electrochemical series
e: The electrochemical series determines the relative ease of discharge of different ions.

q: Cations and anions are arranged in the order of ____ with which they are discharged from solution on passage of electricity.
e: The electrochemical series ranks ions by how readily they gain or lose electrons.

q: This arrangement is known as the ____.
e: The electrochemical series is a list of elements arranged by their standard electrode potentials.

q: It is built up by arranging in order of ____.
e: Electrode potential values quantify the tendency of a species to be reduced or oxidised.

q: If all other factors are equal, any ion ____ will be discharged from the solution in preference to those above it, positive ions at the cathode and negative ions at the anode.
e: Ions lower in the electrochemical series have a greater tendency to be discharged.

q: As the ____, the tendency of the ion to discharge from the solution also increases.
e: Higher ion concentration increases the probability of that ion reaching the electrode and discharging.

q: The order of discharge stated by the electrochemical series may be reversed by the ____.
e: A very high concentration of an ion higher in the series can cause it to discharge preferentially.

q: The discharge of ions during electrolysis can be influenced by the ____.
e: Reactive electrodes can participate in the reaction, altering the expected products of electrolysis.

q: Some electrodes are ____ (do not take part in the electrolytic reaction, e.g., graphite, platinum) while other electrodes are reactive (which may influence the ionic discharge, e.g., copper, mercury and silver).
e: Inert electrodes like platinum and graphite do not react, allowing only the electrolyte ions to discharge.

q: For example, the products of the electrolysis of sodium chloride solution using ____ are quite different.
e: The choice of cathode material can change which cation is preferentially discharged.

q: With platinum cathode, ____ which is lower in the electrochemical series than $Na^+$ ion is discharged.
e: Hydrogen ions are more readily reduced than sodium ions on a platinum surface.

q: If mercury is used as a cathode, $Na^+$ ion is discharged and ____ is produced.
e: Mercury has a high overpotential for hydrogen, allowing sodium ions to discharge and form an amalgam.

q: The aqueous sodium chloride solution contains $Na^+$ and $Cl^-$ ions from the salt, and ____ from water.
e: Water auto-ionises to provide a small concentration of hydrogen and hydroxide ions.

q: On electrolysis, $Na^+$ and $H^+$ ions move to the ____.
e: Cations migrate towards the negatively charged cathode during electrolysis.

q: $H^+$ ion is ____ the $Na^+$ ion on the electrochemical series.
e: Being lower in the series, $H^+$ ions are more easily reduced than $Na^+$ ions.

q: Therefore, $H^+$ ions ____ and are discharged.
e: Reduction at the cathode involves the gain of electrons by the $H^+$ ions.

q: $Cl^-$ ions and $OH^-$ ions move to the ____.
e: Anions migrate towards the positively charged anode during electrolysis.

q: $OH^-$ ion is ____ the $Cl^-$ ion in the electrochemical series.
e: In dilute solutions, $OH^-$ ions are more readily oxidised than $Cl^-$ ions.

q: Therefore, $OH^-$ ions ____ and are discharged.
e: Oxidation at the anode involves the loss of electrons by the $OH^-$ ions.

q: Net result: ____ is evolved at the cathode and oxygen gas is evolved at the anode.
e: Electrolysis of dilute aqueous sodium chloride effectively electrolyses water, producing hydrogen and oxygen.

q: ____ contains $Na^+$ and $Cl^-$ ions from the complete dissociation of sodium chloride, and some $H^+$ and $OH^-$ ions from slight dissociation of water.
e: Brine is a highly concentrated solution of sodium chloride.

q: In brine, $Cl^-$ and $OH^-$ ions move to the ____.
e: Both chloride and hydroxide anions are attracted to the positive anode.

q: The concentration of $Cl^-$ ions is ____ compared to that of $OH^-$ ions.
e: In saturated brine, the high concentration of chloride ions overrides their position in the electrochemical series.

q: Therefore, the $Cl^-$ ions lose electrons and ____ is evolved at the anode.
e: Due to the concentration effect, chloride ions are preferentially discharged to form chlorine gas.

q: Aqueous copper(II) sulphate solution contains ____ from the dissociation of copper(II) sulphate, and $H^+$ and $OH^-$ ions from slight dissociation of water.
e: Copper(II) sulphate dissociates completely into copper and sulphate ions in water.

q: Since $Cu^{2+}$ ion is ____ $H^+$ ion in the electrochemical series, $Cu^{2+}$ ions accept electrons more readily than $H^+$ ions and copper is deposited on the cathode.
e: Copper is less reactive than hydrogen, so its ions are more easily reduced.

q: The colour of solution becomes ____ due to the $H^+$ ions left in the solution.
e: As blue $Cu^{2+}$ ions are removed and $H^+$ ions accumulate, the solution fades and becomes acidic.

q: However, both of these ions are not ____.
e: When reactive copper electrodes are used, the anode itself reacts instead of the anions.

q: Instead of these ions, copper anode is ____.
e: The copper anode oxidises, releasing $Cu^{2+}$ ions into the solution.

q: This is because copper electrodes are ____ and can dissolve in the solution forming $Cu^{2+}$ ions.
e: Reactive anodes participate in the oxidation half-reaction, dissolving into the electrolyte.

q: The effect of the ____ is more prominent than the other two factors when reactive electrodes are used in the electrolysis process.
e: Electrode reactivity can override the electrochemical series and concentration effects.

q: Net result: Copper deposits on the cathode and the ____.
e: The deposition of solid copper adds mass to the cathode.

q: Copper anode dissolves and the ____.
e: The dissolution of the copper anode reduces its mass.

q: The colour of solution ____.
e: Because copper dissolves at the anode at the same rate it deposits at the cathode, the $Cu^{2+}$ concentration remains constant.

q: Sulphuric acid solution contains ____.
e: Dilute sulphuric acid provides hydrogen and sulphate ions, while water provides hydroxide ions.

q: On electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid, $H^+$ ions go to the ____ and accept electrons, and $H_2$ gas is evolved.
e: Hydrogen ions are reduced at the cathode to form hydrogen gas.

q: $SO_4^{2-}$ and $OH^-$ ions both travel to the ____.
e: Anions migrate to the positive anode during electrolysis.

q: $OH^-$ ions ____ and are discharged at the anode.
e: Hydroxide ions are more readily oxidised than sulphate ions.

q: Therefore, ____ is liberated.
e: The oxidation of hydroxide ions produces oxygen gas and water.

q: Net result: ____ are evolved.
c: Two volumes of hydrogen gas and one volume of oxygen gas
e: The stoichiometry of water electrolysis produces hydrogen and oxygen in a 2:1 volume ratio.

q: The solution becomes ____.
e: As water is consumed to produce gases, the remaining sulphuric acid becomes more concentrated.

q: Note: The same result would be obtained from the electrolysis of ____.
e: Electrolysis of dilute alkali also effectively electrolyses water, yielding hydrogen and oxygen.

q: The volume of gases evolved in the electrolysis can be measured by this type of apparatus known as the ____.
e: Hofmann's Voltameter is specifically designed to collect and measure the volumes of gases produced during electrolysis.
